source.title: Jailbreak Transferability Emerges from Shared Representations
source.authors: Rico Angell; Jannik Brinkmann; He He

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or document mismatch.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures cross-model representational similarity and reports that it is limited and can plateau during distillation; it also varies the layer fraction used for the similarity measurement. It does not test whether similarity generally rises as model size or capability increases.
record.gate_note: The paper’s main outcomes concern whether representational similarity predicts jailbreak transfer and whether distillation changes transfer. Those findings are recorded as related results under fits_no_version where they do not measure a convergence version directly. Appendix F varies the representation layer fraction ω, but provides heatmaps without a textual interpretation; those rows are retained as figure-only results. No cited results are recorded as study results.
record.test_reason: The study uses the mutual k-NN metric from the Platonic Representation Hypothesis as a tool to predict jailbreak transfer. It does not test whether independently trained models converge. The similarity rises it reports are produced on purpose by distilling a student on a teacher's outputs. The only natural-similarity data are the Appendix F heatmaps across layer fractions, which are figure-only and never interpreted, plus a passing remark that similarities above 0.5 are rare. None of this is analysed as evidence on convergence, so no version gets a verdict.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely right. The authors conclude that jailbreak transfer emerges from shared representations. Source jailbreak strength and representational similarity predict transfer, and distillation that raises similarity causally increases transfer. They explicitly frame this as aligning with the Platonic Representation Hypothesis, which they assume rather than test. Note that the 'benign-only' distillation also included student refusals to harmful prompts.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the mutual k-nearest-neighbor similarity measure associated with the Platonic Representation Hypothesis, but applies it to instruction-tuned text-only LLMs and jailbreak transfer. It adds a distillation intervention; it does not reproduce the original broad convergence claim or test different modalities.
record.method_sensitivity: The representation layer fraction ω is varied from 0.1 to 1.0 in Appendix F; the heatmaps have no textual interpretation. The main reported measure uses ω=0.8 and k=100. Transfer scores are also reported across source-strength thresholds τ=0.5 to 0.9.

fits_no_version.finding: Across 380 model pairs, mutual k-NN similarity on benign Alpaca prompts is associated with symmetric jailbreak-transfer AUROC. Highly similar pairs never show weak transfer, and the association is tighter among ≥14B models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Representational similarity between LLMs predicts transfer of jailbreaks between them.

fits_no_version.finding: Cross-family SFT distillation on teacher outputs raises teacher–student mutual k-NN similarity by about 0.10–0.14, plateauing early. In-family distillation barely changes it. Distillation also increases jailbreak transfer.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Distillation-induced representational alignment increases jailbreak transferability.

record.problems: The tested models are all text-only decoder-only transformers. Distillation covers only three teacher-student pairs and one epoch with one hyperparameter setting. Similarity is measured with one main metric and fixed main settings; Appendix F provides layer-fraction heatmaps without textual analysis. The text reports no uncertainty estimates for the listed results.

untested.parts: Not tested: no analysis of whether similarity rises with model size or capability. The ≥14B subset concerns the similarity–transfer relationship, not similarity itself.
Not tested: no vision or multimodal models.
Not tested: no mapping or stitching experiments.
Layer fraction is varied only in uninterpreted heatmaps. Metric, k and input data are never varied.
Not analysed: neither the incompleteness of natural alignment nor its causes are examined. The family-related remarks are speculative and concern distillation.

missing.what: Figure 2 splits pairs into same-family and different-family groups, and Figure 12 shows a PCA of models clustering by family. Either could bear on shared-data explanations of similarity, but neither is interpreted in text.

record.verdict_notes: Relation changed from tests/T5 to uses_without_test/T4. The convergence-related rows either reflect alignment induced on purpose by distillation or are uninterpreted figures, so the reader's V7 labels are removed.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test whether independently trained models become more similar as size or capability increases. Its ≥14B subset concerns the relationship between similarity and transfer AUROC, not whether similarity rises with scale.
No vision-language models or paired image-caption representations are tested.
The paper does not compare same-architecture models across random seeds or test shared features or subspaces.
No mapping, stitching, relative-representation, or unpaired interchangeability experiment is reported.
No recurring interpretable features or circuits are identified across models.
The paper varies layer fraction ω in Appendix F. It does not compare different similarity metrics, vary k in the reported experiment, compare input datasets, or test out-of-distribution inputs.

The study reports limited similarity and plateaus during selected distillations, plus a family-distillation control. It does not causally establish that shared training data or objectives, rather than a common model of reality, explain general convergence.

rows.subject: 380 pairs of the 20 open-weight models (aggregate)
rows.size_stated: 500 million to 70 billion parameters across the studied models
rows.operation_detail: Compared pairwise mutual k-nearest-neighbor representation similarity with symmetric jailbreak-transfer AUROC.

conditions.value: last-token hidden states at 0.8 × depth; 10K Alpaca prompts

rows.measure: Relationship between pairwise representation similarity and symmetric transfer AUROC
rows.value: Text reports that highly similar model pairs never had weak transfer; the relationship was tighter among pairs where both models had at least 14B parameters.
rows.locator: Figure 2 and Section 4, “Transfer AUROC increases with model similarity”
rows.note: The reported outcome is the association with jailbreak transfer, not a size-related increase in representational similarity.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-7B distilled from Llama3.1-8B
rows.stage_stated: SFT for one epoch; teacher responses to benign Alpaca instructions plus student refusal responses to harmful instructions
rows.operation_detail: Measured teacher-student mutual k-nearest-neighbor similarity during distillation.
rows.value: Increase of 0.10–0.12 (the paper groups this with the other two pairs; it does not give this pair’s separate exact gain in text)
rows.locator: Figure 4 and Section 5, “Distillation increases model similarity”
rows.note: The text says similarity rises sharply early and then plateaus. This distillation included student-generated harmful-prompt refusals, not only benign data.
rows.check: Similarity is deliberately raised by distilling on teacher outputs, so this is not convergence arising in independently trained models. The plateau describes a one-epoch SFT run, not the limits of natural alignment.

rows.subject: In-family distillations (aggregate; example given: Llama3.1-8B into Llama3.2-3B)
rows.size_stated: not stated for the aggregate control
rows.operation_detail: Compared representation similarity before and after in-family distillation.
rows.note: The authors suggest representational capacity may limit alignment and note that smaller family models may already be distilled or trained on the same data.
rows.check: In-family distillation control within an induced-alignment experiment. It does not measure convergence of independently trained models.

rows.subject: 20 open-weight models (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Reported the observed range of pairwise representation similarities.
rows.value: The authors state that similarities larger than 0.5 are rarely observed.
rows.note: This supports the paper’s qualification that measured alignment is limited, rather than complete.
rows.check: A passing remark used to argue that the distillation gains are substantial. No distribution or analysis of natural similarity is given, and no ceiling or plateau claim is made about convergence.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Reported cross-family distillation similarity results and overall similarity range
reader_labels.reason: Similarity rises but is described as rarely exceeding 0.5, and the authors report early plateaus; this supports a qualification that alignment is incomplete rather than complete (R2–R4, R6).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: In-family distillation has almost no effect on similarity, so the reported increase is not uniform across distillation settings (R5).
